clue.text: Pants for mum

parts.note: 'for' can mean 'to', as in 'a present for you' / 'to you'
'mum' means silent, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing underwear bought as a gift for their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British slang for rubbish or nonsense, not trousers or underwear here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang words for worthless nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Doggedness shown by number one team from Manchester

parts.note: ten is a number
a means one, as in 'a dozen'
City is Manchester City football club

explanation.surface: Persistence displayed by the top football side in Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' reads as the top team, but splits into TEN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is persistence and determination, the quality of not letting go.

clue.text: Oscar-winning Kevin Costner for starters is backing Michael Moore film

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the gathered letters are read from the end
starters are first courses, so only the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: An award-winning star supporting a documentary by Michael Moore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is backing' does double work: 'is' gives IS, then the whole OKC + IS is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicko is Michael Moore's 2007 documentary about the American health care system.

clue.text: Working boy's suspicious behaviour

parts.note: a going concern is one that is working or operating
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a lad who has a job is up to something dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'boy' is just 'has' or 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are shady or improper activities, the kind of conduct that arouses suspicion.

clue.text: What supervisor has to do during the main broadcast

parts.note: over means during, as in 'over the weekend'

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so a word that sounds the same is meant

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: A supervisor's duty during a programme going out on the main channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervising is watching over and directing the work of others.

clue.text: Make out sylvan area

parts.note: to make out is to kiss and cuddle, which in British slang is to neck
sylvan means belonging to the woods

explanation.surface: Lovers kissing in a woodland clearing.
explanation.definitionFit: One's neck of the woods is the local area or district where one lives.

clue.text: Rogue caught cracking safe's about to face term in jail

indicators.note: to face something is to stand before it, so the pieces come first
cracking open means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sound means safe, as in 'safe and sound'; the 's is 'has'
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a term is an end, so the end of the prison word is taken

explanation.surface: A villain nabbed while breaking into a safe is about to be sentenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' and 'cracking' build a safe-breaking story, but 'safe' means SOUND, which C breaks into.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel and a rogue are both dishonest, unprincipled people.

clue.text: Curious numbers close to infinity

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Odd numbers that come near infinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' looks like strange, but here means inquisitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy person is inquisitive, prying into others' business.

clue.text: Time to visit Chilean cities after working out minor details

indicators.note: a visitor arrives at a place, so this piece comes along before the rest
working out means solving or reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A travel plan to tour Chile's cities once the small print is sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: Technicalities are small formal points or details, often of procedure.

clue.text: The last thing Picasso drew?

parts.note: 'drew' looks like sketching, but a dying person draws a final lungful of air

explanation.surface: A quiz on the artist's final sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: When someone dies they are said to draw their last lungful of air.

clue.text: Rear view of a Parisian with carrots and cereal for treating piles

indicators.note: a view from the rear sees the word back to front, so the French article is turned round

parts.note: a Parisian would say 'un' for 'a'

indicators.note: treating means processing or working on, so the letters of the two vegetables-and-grain words are reworked

explanation.surface: A spoof remedy for haemorrhoids: a French view of carrots and cereal as a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piles' looks medical, but an atomic pile is an old name for a nuclear reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: Early nuclear reactors were called atomic piles, from the stacked graphite blocks of the first ones.

clue.text: Dimwit pays heed? Not this one

parts.note: a clot is a stupid person, a dimwit
someone who hears takes notice, pays heed

explanation.surface: Asks whether the fool is listening, then answers that this one is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not this one' points back at 'pays heed': the answer is British slang for someone who never listens.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone 'cloth ears' is a British jibe at a person who does not listen, so does not pay heed.

clue.text: Maintaining wife, supported by special grants

indicators.note: maintaining means keeping hold of, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: something resting on another is supported by it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a spouse thanks to particular government grants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grants' is a verb meaning admits or concedes, not money handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a fact is to admit or concede it, just as one grants a point in argument.

clue.text: Rock star in hot spot

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters of these words are jolted into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A rock musician staying in a sweltering location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock star' reads as one phrase, but 'Rock' scrambles STAR IN to TARNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to stain or blemish it, which is what tarnishing does.

clue.text: Dicky let one rip in overabundant fullness

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a dodgy stomach breaks wind after overeating.
explanation.definitionFit: Repletion is the state of being completely full, especially after eating too much.

clue.text: Whole collection of books discovered in Ireland

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A complete set of volumes turns up in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entire is complete, with nothing missing, the same sense as whole.

clue.text: Wizard briefly seen in Novgorod

parts.note: the short form VG, the usual abbreviation, sits inside the city name Novgorod

explanation.surface: A sorcerer glimpsed for a moment in the Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' means in abbreviated form: the answer's abbreviation VG is in the middle of NoVGorod.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Wizard' is dated British slang for excellent, splendid.

clue.text: Superman will occasionally sit in an ungainly manner

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Even the Man of Steel sometimes slumps awkwardly in a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to sit or lie with limbs spread out awkwardly.

clue.text: Funny tingle round freckle

indicators.note: funny means peculiar, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An odd tingling sensation around a mole on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentigo is a small flat brown spot on the skin, the medical term for a freckle.

clue.text: The sound of Take That is coming from this alley

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so a word spelt differently but said the same is meant

parts.note: to take something is to steal it
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Music by the boy band Take That is drifting out of a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alley' is not a lane but a marble, and a steelie is a steel marble.
explanation.definitionFit: Alley and steelie are both kinds of playing marble, the first originally of alabaster, the second of steel.

clue.text: Do 16d and 1a in class

parts.note: the clue at 16 down means very good, and 'so' stands for very, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the class abbreviation

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
read as it looks, 1a is the letters I and A, the figure 1 standing for I

explanation.surface: An instruction to put two crossword answers into a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: '1a' is not the across clue but the literal letters IA, 1 standing for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a party or gathering, and so is a social.

clue.text: Type of shop that made lip-smacking sandwiches

indicators.note: the words sandwich the answer between them, holding it in their letters

explanation.surface: A delicatessen that once made delicious sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and sandwiches.

clue.text: Rolls Royce with long death announcement

indicators.note: rolls means turns over, so the letters of the two words tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce with a lengthy obituary notice, as at a grand funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls Royce' reads as the car, but 'Rolls' is the anagram signal for ROYCE LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A necrology is an obituary notice or a register of deaths.

clue.text: One eyes untidy glory hole overlooking holy ground

indicators.note: untidy means messy, so the letters of the two-word phrase are thrown about
overlooking means leaving out, so some letters of the jumble are ignored
ground means crushed, so the letters of the sacred word are broken up too

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a messy junk cupboard that looks down on a sacred site.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumble GLORY HOLE, ignore the scrambled letters of HOLY, and the remaining O, G, L, E, R rearrange. A glory hole is a British term for a junk cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who eyes others, especially leeringly, is someone who ogles.

clue.text: Eccentric earl dispensed with stick

indicators.note: dispensed with means done without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a flake is informal, chiefly American, for an eccentric or unreliable person

explanation.surface: An odd aristocrat stopped using his walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' is not a cane but criticism, as in 'taking stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for harsh criticism, as in 'getting a lot of flak'.

clue.text: Writer's guild negotiated with April O'Neil

indicators.note: terms that are negotiated are worked over and rearranged, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A writers' union bargaining with someone called April O'Neil.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Writer' is 'is'; the fodder is GUILD plus APRIL O'NEIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian dramatist and novelist, author of Six Characters in Search of an Author and a Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Man accompanies boy round the northern capital

indicators.note: accompanies means goes alongside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts, and the king is one

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the boy word goes about the short article

parts.note: a son is a boy
in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t', as in 'on t' moor'

explanation.surface: An adult escorts a lad around the capital of the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern' looks part of the definition; it says T is the Yorkshire form of 'the'. Kingston is the capital of Jamaica.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingston is the capital city of Jamaica.

clue.text: Raised money during speech

indicators.note: in speech only the sound counts, so a word that is spoken the same but spelt differently is meant

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Funds were raised while someone was giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals or children that were raised were brought up or reared.
